summary.name: Vaporwave, a supplemental Digital and 3D Aesthetics design reference. The source does not name it as a directly named style in its collection, and it must stay distinct from Synthwave.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: combines nostalgic consumer imagery, early digital interfaces, sculpture, or advertising fragments with a coherent pastel palette and selective distortion. It favors slow repetition, drift, and displaced time. A recognizable theme must be kept.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: vaporwave alone suits slow nostalgic loops. Listed compatible fits include editorial narratives, product explainers, document or process sequences, and flat vector, collage, sticker, or motion-poster layouts. Inferred: music visuals and editorial art pieces, as the combinations suggest. Any other use is unspecified.
summary.limitations: Explicit: adapt or omit it when the stack hides content the viewer must read, when overlap obscures provenance or comparison labels, or when fixed print geometry cannot fit the stacking. Avoid fast, driving Synthwave pacing. Two-color contrast checks do not verify text over images, textures, video, or animated lighting.
summary.palette: Authored suggestion, not supplied, for new artwork only when no approved palette exists: background #EAE0F0, foreground #474257, accent_1 #CE9BB8, accent_2 #8DBBB8, accent_3 #B2A4D0. Gradients are disabled. Task, brand, or reference colors override these. Foreground on background is 7.515:1. Accent_2 with foreground is 4.546:1, which passes. Accent_1 and accent_3 (4.122:1 and 4.171:1) are decorative fills only.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: slow drift and repetition, with occasional local distortion driven from deterministic time. Optional motion references are motion-008 (card stacking), motion-012 (chaptered handoff), and motion-015 (narrative storytelling), each usable only if the scene supports its action. Interactive delivery may use scroll and a reduced-motion option that freezes drift. Video must stay independent of live input.
summary.audio: Unspecified by the style. The source assigns no fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or mandatory audio layer. Music, voiceover, sung vocals, effects, ambience, or silence should be proposed per topic and scene, with reasons. Explicit user audio choices and supplied assets take priority, and no audio assets should be invented. Speech intelligibility and picture sync must be verified.
summary.assetRequirements: Explicit: supplied or licensed imagery is required, including consumer, advertising, sculptural, or photographic fragments. Hybrids depend on supplied assets, and unlicensed brand logos are to be avoided. Layered assets need preserved transparency, consistent dimensions, clear naming, and inspection before composition. Fonts and assets must be loaded before rendering. Specific fonts are unspecified.
summary.combinations: Explicit: collage style-044 supplies consumer fragments tinted toward the primary accent tokens, with slow deterministic drift, for nostalgia music visuals and editorial art. Symmetric staging style-104 supplies a centered, mirrored composition for album-art loops and gallery pieces. Both avoid fast Synthwave pacing. Avoid busy asymmetric clutter and neon grids with style-104.
summary.productionApproach: Explicit ownership: Canvas 2D and layered assets handle visual construction, with optional PixiJS for large sprite or particle sets driven from fixed video time. HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for timing, sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. GSAP provides the paused timeline. Chroma.js is optional for palette checks. Seed randomness, cache simulations, and verify decoded frames and loop seams. Simulated appearance is not physical production evidence.
